metaDescription: Own coalbed methane minerals near Hoehne, Las Animas County? We price Raton Basin interests off your actual production history.
heroLead: Hoehne sits just outside Trinidad in the Colorado Raton Basin, coalbed methane country where wells have quietly produced from the Vermejo and Raton coal seams for over two decades.
intro: Las Animas County mineral ownership around Hoehne often connects to old ranching and coal-town family land, with some tracts holding both a mining history and, separately, an active oil and gas lease tied to coalbed methane production.
The Raton Basin's slow, steady decline behavior means many interests here have been paying modest royalties consistently for years, which gives us solid trailing data to price against.

sections.heading: The long tail of Raton Basin wells
paragraphs: Coalbed methane wells decline more gradually than horizontal shale wells once past their initial dewatering phase, which is why a Hoehne-area interest that has been producing for fifteen or twenty years can still carry meaningful value. We fit a decline curve to your actual check stub trend rather than assuming a short remaining life.

sections.heading: Confirming what your deed actually covers
paragraphs: Given the area's coal mining history, some older deeds separate coal rights from oil and gas rights. We review your specific deed language before pricing to confirm exactly what mineral interest you hold.

sections.heading: Title research through Las Animas County
paragraphs: We verify leases, unit agreements, and any prior assignments through the Las Animas County Clerk and Recorder, since Raton Basin assets have changed operators several times over the decades and we want your net revenue interest confirmed against current records.

sections.heading: What a Hoehne offer actually reflects
paragraphs: An offer on your Hoehne-area interest reflects your net revenue interest, the well's current position on its decline curve, and recent comparable Raton Basin sales in Las Animas County. We walk through each of those three inputs with you so the number is not a mystery.

faqs.question: How long can a Raton Basin well near Hoehne keep producing?
faqs.answer: Many wells in this field have produced for two decades or more thanks to a gradual, long-tail decline pattern typical of coalbed methane.

faqs.question: Does my deed cover both coal and oil and gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. We check your specific deed language to confirm exactly what you own before making an offer.

faqs.question: My royalty checks list a different operator than a few years ago. Should I worry?
faqs.answer: No, this basin has changed operators multiple times. We confirm the current operator before finalizing your offer.

faqs.question: Can you explain how you arrived at my specific offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, we walk through net revenue interest, decline curve position, and comparable sales so you understand exactly how the number was built.
